rows.grounds: names sesame as a standard of measure in the listed sequence
names mustard seed as a standard of measure in the listed sequence
names turmeric as a standard of measure in the listed sequence
compound of go and śakṛt naming cow-dung as a standard of measure
names ash as a standard of measure in the listed sequence
designates the preceding items as constituting the prescribed measure

items.question: Which substances constitute the prescribed standard of measure in this sequence?
premises: The preceding verses establish specific measures for materials such as rice, sugar, and fragrant substances.
Sesame, mustard, turmeric, cow-dung, and ash are enumerated together in this verse.
The term mānakam designates these enumerated substances as a standard of measure.
items.inference: Therefore, sesame, mustard, turmeric, cow-dung, and ash together constitute the prescribed measure in this context.
uncertainties: Whether mānakam refers to a single composite measure or to alternative measures is not explicitly specified.
items.plain_english: Sesame, mustard, turmeric, cow-dung, and ash are the prescribed measure.
